title: A Hierarchical Context Augmentation Method to Improve Retrieval-Augmented LLMs on Scientific Papers

problem.claim: Retrieval-Augmented LLMs need to better utilize the hierarchical structure of scientific papers to grasp their central thought.

gap.claim: Existing methods capture one-dimensional fragmented textual information without incorporating hierarchical structural knowledge, such as the deduction relationship between abstracts and main bodies.

contributions.claim: A hierarchical context augmentation method helps Retrieval-Augmented LLMs autoregressively learn the structural knowledge of scientific papers.
The method represents papers with document trees and enhances scientific-context structure through scale, format, and global information.
The method uses top-bottom document-tree paths as independent contexts, a label-based structural format unified across training and inference, and global information from retrieved passages.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the label-based format for representing context structure in textual sequences as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments on three scientific tasks significantly improve Retrieval-Augmented LLM performance on all tasks.
The authors report state-of-the-art performance on a question-answering task and performance exceeding ChatGPT.
The authors report gains when retrieval passages are irrelevant, which they associate with practical application scenarios.

narrative_sequence.summary: Scientific papers provide substantial data and knowledge, motivating methods that can use large scientific corpora.
Existing Retrieval-Augmented LLM methods use fragmented one-dimensional information and miss hierarchical relationships needed to capture a paper's central thought.
The proposed approach augments retrieval contexts with document-tree structure through scale, a unified label-based format, and global passage information.
The authors report improvements across three scientific tasks, strong question-answering results, and gains with irrelevant retrieval passages.

source_observation.claim: The method organizes scientific-paper context using hierarchical document-tree relationships and top-bottom paths.

interpretation.claim: Preserving document hierarchy may help retrieval-augmented systems represent relationships that fragmented passages omit.

application.claim: When building retrieval-augmented systems for structured documents, represent retrieved content together with relevant hierarchical context.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the approach generalizes beyond scientific papers or which structural components are necessary.

source_observation.claim: The authors report gains even with irrelevant retrieval passages.

interpretation.claim: Structural context augmentation may provide robustness when retrieval quality is imperfect.

application.claim: Evaluate retrieval-augmented systems under noisy or irrelevant retrieval conditions when practical robustness matters.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the amount or type of retrieval noise used in the experiments.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide dataset names, baselines, metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not describe ablations or isolate the effects of scale, format, and global information.
The abstract does not report implementation details, computational cost, or limitations.
